why:
Perched on act-latecomer, added at seq 15 and not placed until seq 17 -- by which time (3,0) has been opened AND shut again. So this seat never sees past it, and act-hidden, being non-party, is never introduced by the roster either: THIS LOG DOES NOT KNOW act-hidden EXISTS. Its ability use, resource change and condition are all absent.

Two different gates produce that one outcome, and the distinction matters to anyone porting these arms. resourceChanged and conditionApplied are passIf(pr.actors[id]) -- forwarded only to a viewer that ALREADY HELD the actor. abilityUsed is passIf(knows(...)), which is pr.actors OR now.actors -- and now.actors is NOT merely what is visible: look fills it from visible tokens AND from every party member, so a party member two rooms away is known and unseen. That is what makes knows() deliberately weaker, so testimony about an actor being introduced on the same event still arrives. Here they agree only because this seat never holds act-hidden at all.

It also never learns that (5,0) was opened, and the reason is NOT geometry. At seq 12 act-latecomer is not yet in st.Actors at all, so the spectator arm of eyes returns nil, look yields an empty square set, and every sight-gated arm fails for want of eyes rather than for want of a line. (3,0) becomes the reason only from seq 17, once this seat is placed -- which is why no correction is ever owed afterwards either. Its OpenDoors is empty while act-watcher's holds (5,0) -- two seats in one corridor disagreeing about the state of the world, which is the whole point of a per-character log.

What DOES reach it from before it existed: the sitting, and the party roster, which is why this stream names act-watcher. Roster-gated exposure, recorded by the plan as a product question rather than a sight leak.

THIS IS NOT TASK 15's SCENARIO, and should not be mistaken for it. Task 15 asks for two characters present throughout and a third who joins partway AND LEAVES BEFORE THE END, whose log starts at join and simply stops. This seat only arrives late; it never leaves, there is one party member present throughout rather than two, and its oracle starts at world event 1. The departure half -- ActorRemoved reaching only the seat that held the actor, and a log that stops -- is still uncovered.

This directory is also sub-project 14's ORACLE for act-latecomer.
